summary: Quote latency degradation in INC-006 is best explained by H1: market-data-service itself slowed, and that slowdown propagated up the quote path into pricing-engine and on to order-service / api-gateway trading screens (confidence 0.50, medium — clearly ahead of H2 0.30 and H3 0.25). The evidence is consistent and multi-source: pricing-engine's p99 jumped from ~60ms to >2.2s between the 13:08 and 13:16 buckets while its own CPU (39-40%) and memory (48-49%) stayed flat, and 192/197 of its error logs name market-data-service as the timed-out downstream, with market-data-service's own p99 independently rising from ~40ms to ~1.7-2.0s in the same 13:12-13:21 window. No deployment or config change touched pricing-engine or any quote-path service; the only change in the window (auth-service v7.2.0 at 11:30Z, SameSite=strict) is off the pricing path and unsupported by telemetry. Confidence is capped at medium because the intrinsic cause inside market-data-service was never resolved — its slowdown could still be inherited from redis-cache (H2) or the external exchange-api via exchange-gateway (H3), and those telemetry checks were not completed.

ranked_hypotheses.title: market-data-service itself slowed (dependency degradation on the quote path)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: pricing-engine's downstream market-data-service experienced its own latency degradation starting 13:12-13:21Z, which propagated as quote deadline-exceeded errors in pricing-engine, and on to order-service/api-gateway trading screens. The fault origin is market-data-service (or something immediately behind it), not pricing-engine.

causal_chain.claim: market-data-service p99 jumps from ~40ms to ~1700-1980ms in the 13:21 bucket, same window as the pricing-engine latency jump
pricing-engine emits 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' (192/197 matched logs), naming market-data-service as the slow downstream
pricing-engine p99 jumps ~60ms -> 601ms -> 2211ms and 5xx rises to ~4% with flat CPU/memory, i.e. no local saturation
Latency propagates to order-service/api-gateway and thus the trading screens
No deployment or config change to pricing-engine, market-data, cache or broker in the window, so the origin is an intrinsic/operational failure inside market-data-service or its own upstreams

assumptions: market-data-service's slowdown is intrinsic (own resource/GC/thread-pool/connection issue) rather than purely inherited from exchange-gateway/exchange-api/redis-cache; this distinction was never resolved (GAP: market-data-service log query not executed)
The 13:12-13:21 onset in market-data-service is real and not an artifact of a delayed/misaligned metric bucket

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared redis-cache degradation/cold-cache storm slows the quote path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The shared redis-cache (platform-owned, consumed by auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service) degraded or lost its warm dataset, causing cache-miss storms that inflated market-data-service and pricing-engine quote latency. Origin is redis-cache (infrastructure), consistent with the HIST-107 precedent.

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache is the only shared node in the quote dependency graph, feeding both market-data-service and pricing-engine directly
A redis-cache failure/failover or cold cache would inflate downstream reads on both market-data-service and pricing-engine simultaneously
market-data-service p99 rises to ~1700-1980ms and pricing-engine attributes deadline-exceeded to market-data-service
Symptom pattern matches precedent HIST-107 'Cold cache storm after redis failover' on redis-cache + market-data-service with 'quote latency'

assumptions: redis-cache actually degraded at 13:12-13:21 (no redis metrics were retrieved on this path)
redis-cache is a single point of failure / has a replica/failover event; its redundancy model is unknown
The HIST-107 precedent is relevant despite being from a past incident and explicitly flagged as a 'lead only'

ranked_hypotheses.title: External exchange-api / exchange-gateway slowdown propagating up the quote path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: exchange-gateway's call to the external exchange-api (type=external, has_telemetry=false) degraded, slowing market-data-service, then pricing-engine, then order-service and the screens. Origin is the external provider or the exchange-gateway edge.

causal_chain.claim: Full quote path is pricing-engine -> market-data-service -> exchange-gateway -> exchange-api
An external exchange slowdown would raise exchange-gateway and then market-data-service latency
market-data-service p99 rises to ~1700-1980ms in the 13:21 bucket, matching the pricing-engine deadline-exceeded signature naming market-data-service
Precedent HIST-103 'external exchange partner outage causing upstream timeouts' matches this failure point

assumptions: exchange-api is degraded; it has no telemetry so this cannot be observed (explicit GAP)
exchange-gateway metrics were never retrieved, so no direct evidence links this hop to the 13:12-13:21 onset

ranked_hypotheses.title: auth-service v7.2.0 (SameSite=strict) is the trigger (reporter-adjacent / only-change-in-window suspect)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only deployment in the entire window, auth-service v7.2.0 'Session cookie hardening' at 11:30Z, changed session cookie behavior in a way that disrupted shared traffic or the shared redis-cache (e.g. session re-authentication storm or cache-key churn), indirectly slowing the quote path.

causal_chain.claim: auth-service v7.2.0 (SameSite=strict) is the only deployment in 2026-04-08 00:00Z - 2026-04-09 14:59Z, live and never rolled back
auth-service shares redis-cache with pricing-engine and market-data-service
A cookie-policy change causing session churn could add load to the shared redis-cache, slowing quote reads
market-data-service / pricing-engine latency then rises

assumptions: auth-service session churn measurably loads the shared redis-cache on the quote path (no supporting telemetry)
The 11:30Z deploy's effect manifested ~1h45m later at 13:08-13:16 without any intermediate signal

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine-internal saturation (resources / pools / retry storm)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: pricing-engine itself is the origin: its own CPU/memory/pool saturation or a retry storm caused the p99 and 5xx degradation, and the market-data-service slow hop is a secondary symptom of pricing-engine's own retries.

causal_chain.claim: pricing-engine p99 and 5xx rise sharply at 13:16-13:21
Its own compute is saturated or its connection pool is exhausted
Errors quote 'market-data-service took Nms' because pricing-engine's own overload delayed its outbound calls

assumptions: The downstream-attributed timeout messages are misleading rather than descriptive
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: pricing-engine CPU (39-40%) and memory (48-49%) are flat with no step change at onset (F16); 192/197 logs attribute the exceeded deadline to market-data-service, and market-data-service's own p99 independently rises in the same bucket (F17); no deployment (F1) or config change (F11) touched pricing-engine. Own-saturation is contradicted by the evidence.

facts.statement: pricing-engine p99 latency was flat at ~59-62ms through the 13:08 bucket, then jumped in the 13:16 bucket to avg 601.68ms / max 2227.82ms and stayed elevated (13:24 avg 2211.36ms). Onset is between 13:08 and 13:16 UTC.

market-data-service p99 latency was flat at ~39-40ms through the 13:12 bucket, then jumped in the same 13:21 bucket to avg 1702.29ms / max 1979.98ms (13:30 avg 1814.5ms), placing its own latency onset in the 13:12-13:21 window.

The dominant pricing-engine error signature is 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' at 192 of 197 matched logs, with observed durations 827ms to 8456ms; first ERROR log 13:23:57Z. No 5xx/connection-refused pattern appears in the top patterns.
pricing-engine error_rate rose from ~0.17-0.24% (13:12 bucket) to avg 3.32% / max 4.37% in the 13:21 bucket and held ~4%; the 5xx elevation begins in the same bucket as the latency jump.

pricing-engine's own CPU stayed ~39-40% (max 44.48, min 34.59) and memory ~48-49% (max 54.93, min 43.36) from 12:00 through 14:51 with no step change at 13:16-13:21, indicating no CPU or memory saturation in pricing-engine itself.

The quote path is pricing-engine -> market-data-service (http) and pricing-engine -> redis-cache (cache), with market-data-service depending on redis-cache (cache) and exchange-gateway (http), which in turn calls external exchange-api.

redis-cache is the only 'shared' datastore in pricing-engine's dependency graph (owner=platform, type=redis, shared=true) and is consumed by auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service.

Latency propagates onward from pricing-engine: order-service -> pricing-engine (http) and api-gateway -> order-service -> pricing-engine, so pricing latency reaches the trading screens behind api-gateway.

A full all-services deployment sweep from 2026-04-08T00:00Z to 2026-04-09T14:59Z returns exactly one deployment: auth-service v7.2.0 'Session cookie hardening' (SameSite=strict) at 11:30Z, status live, never rolled back; no deployment touched pricing-engine or any market-data/quote/cache/broker service.

All-services config/feature-flag change sweeps for 2026-04-08 to 2026-04-09 (and a pricing-engine-scoped query) return zero changes; no timeout, pool-size, flag, cache-TTL or routing config change was recorded around the incident window.
Precedent HIST-107 (2025-12-09) 'Cold cache storm after redis failover' involved redis-cache and market-data-service with symptom 'quote latency'; recorded as a lead only, not evidence.

Other precedents (HIST-113 market-open volume exceeding provisioned capacity, HIST-115 connection pool misconfiguration, HIST-110 ledger-db IOPS throttling) match symptoms but have different recorded causes; recorded as leads only.

assumptions: Assumption: market-data-service's slowdown is intrinsic (its own resource/GC/thread-pool/connection issue) rather than purely inherited from redis-cache, exchange-gateway or external exchange-api; this distinction was never resolved because the market-data-service log query was not executed.
Assumption: the 13:12-13:21 onset in market-data-service is real and not an artifact of a delayed or misaligned metric bucket.
Assumption: redis-cache is on the critical quote path for market-data-service such that its degradation could produce the observed market-data-service slowdown (H2 remains viable but unmeasured).

Assumption: exchange-gateway/exchange-api sits on the quote path and could slow market-data-service, but no exchange-gateway metrics or external telemetry were retrieved (H3 remains viable but unmeasured).
Assumption: the deployment and config-change sweeps are complete enough to exclude a change-driven trigger despite one backend shard not responding on the first attempt.
Assumption: the 13:16-13:21 onset windows observed for pricing-engine and market-data-service reflect the same causal event rather than two unrelated degradations.

recommended_actions.action: Mitigate at the quote-path bottleneck: check and warm/restore the redis-cache dataset consumed by market-data-service on the quote path (if hit-rate/evictions or a failover-to-empty-replica pattern is present, warm the cache and re-point to the healthy primary).
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 is the leading alternative to H1 and redis-cache is the only shared node on the quote path (F3, F8) with a matching precedent (F5). If redis-cache is the true bottleneck, warming/restoring it stops the degradation immediately; this is safe even if H1 is the true cause.

recommended_actions.action: Mitigate at market-data-service: verify its health (thread-pool/connection-pool/GC and dependency timeouts) and, if it is the bottleneck, shed or scale it (increase replicas / restart the degraded instance) to restore market-data-service p99 toward its ~40ms baseline.
recommended_actions.rationale: H1 is the top-ranked hypothesis (0.50): market-data-service's own p99 jumped to ~1.7-2.0s in the same window (F17) and is named as the slow downstream in 192/197 pricing-engine errors (F14). Reducing its latency directly relieves pricing-engine and the trading screens (F9).

recommended_actions.action: Protect the downstream chain while mitigations are applied: raise/relax the pricing-engine quote deadline temporarily and/or enable the fallback/cached-quote path so order-service and api-gateway screens do not surface 3s loads and 5xx.
recommended_actions.rationale: Degradation propagates pricing-engine -> order-service -> api-gateway to the trading screens (F9), with pricing-engine error_rate holding ~4% (F15). A temporary deadline/fallback change limits customer-visible impact without masking the root cause.

recommended_actions.action: Discriminate H1 vs H2 vs H3 by collecting the missing telemetry: market-data-service WARN+ logs; redis-cache node metrics (memory, evictions, hit-rate, connections, latency, failover events); exchange-gateway latency/error metrics and exchange-api call outcomes for the 13:00-13:30 window.
recommended_actions.rationale: These checks were never executed (budget exhausted) and are exactly what separates an intrinsic market-data-service slowdown from inherited redis-cache or exchange degradation (F3, F7). Confirming the true origin avoids re-occurrence.

recommended_actions.action: After the immediate bottleneck is relieved, verify recovery: confirm market-data-service p99 returns to ~40ms and pricing-engine p99 returns to ~60ms with 5xx back to ~0.2% over at least 15-30 minutes, then close the incident.
recommended_actions.rationale: Provides an objective exit criterion against the observed baselines and onset profile (F13, F15, F17).

recommended_actions.action: Add capacity/headroom and dependency-health guardrails on the quote path: per-dependency latency SLOs and alerting for market-data-service, redis-cache hit-rate/eviction and exchange-gateway/exchange-api timeouts, plus pre-scaling for market-open volume.
recommended_actions.rationale: The incident spread silently for ~8 minutes before pricing-engine breached (F13, F15) and the origin could not be localized because downstream dependency telemetry was absent (gaps in redis-cache, exchange-gateway and market-data-service logs). Precedents HIST-113 (market-open capacity) and HIST-107 (redis failover cold cache) show recurring failure modes at these points (F5, F6).

recommended_actions.action: Ensure request-scoped instrumentation records which dependency consumes the deadline budget (a per-hop tracer or structured 'slow_dependency' field), so the root hop is unambiguous in future incidents.
recommended_actions.rationale: Currently the only attribution is free-text log messages (F14), which forced this investigation to rely on inference rather than direct evidence.

data_gaps: market-data-service WARN+ log query was never executed, so its own error/exception signature and the intrinsic cause of its slowdown are unconfirmed — this is why H1 is capped at medium confidence.
No redis-cache telemetry was retrieved (memory, evictions, hit-rate, connection count, latency, failover/replica events) and its redundancy model is unknown, so H2 cannot be excluded or confirmed.
exchange-gateway metrics were never retrieved and exchange-api is type=external with has_telemetry=false, so H3 cannot be excluded or confirmed.

Only pricing-engine and market-data-service were probed for latency; api-gateway, order-service, portfolio-service, exchange-gateway, ledger-db, redis-cache and kafka were not checked for the same 13:16-13:21 window, so the full set of co-affected services is unknown.
Quote-endpoint granularity (uniform vs isolated across quote endpoints/routes) was not tested, so it is unknown whether the latency is uniform across all quote paths.
No GC, thread-pool or connection-pool metrics were retrieved for pricing-engine (and request_rate/restarts were not queried), so the 'no own-saturation' verdict rests only on CPU and memory flatness.
The first all-services deployment query returned partial=true with a non-responding backend shard, so an unlisted early-window deployment on that shard cannot be fully excluded.

The config-change store returned zero for all services and it is unknown whether infra/network/mesh changes are even recorded there, so absence of config changes may reflect a recording gap rather than genuinely no changes.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: If market-data-service is shown to be healthy on its own (flat internal resource/thread/connection metrics) while redis-cache metrics show evictions, hit-rate collapse or a failover-to-empty-replica event at 13:12-13:21, the conclusion shifts to H2 (redis-cache) as the origin.
If exchange-gateway/exchange-api call timeouts or latency are shown to rise starting at/near 13:12-13:21 and precede market-data-service's slowdown, the conclusion shifts to H3 (external exchange).

If a deployment or config change on a previously unreported shard (the partial first sweep) is found touching market-data-service or redis-cache in this window, a deployment-triggered hypothesis would need re-ranking.

If market-data-service's own resource metrics show CPU/memory/thread-pool/connection-pool saturation at onset, that would convert H1 from 'a dependency slowed' to a specific intrinsic resource-exhaustion root cause within market-data-service.
If per-hop tracing shows the pricing-engine deadline budget being consumed inside pricing-engine itself (not by market-data-service), the rejection of H5 would need revisiting.
